subject: Pro forma payment plan request — Atlas Health
messages:
From: Emily Cho <emily.cho@atlashealth.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Kline <ben.kline@atlashealth.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Aug 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed invoice schedule for enterprise contract

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks again for the conversation yesterday. Our procurement team has asked us to propose a payment plan that aligns with our fiscal cadence. They are requesting Net-90 terms or a split quarterly invoicing schedule (three installments over 9 months) for the initial annual commitment.

We realize this is non-standard — Atlas is moving its ERP cutover and the CFO prefers the longer window to keep cashflows aligned. We can provide a PO in advance and are comfortable committing to the contract effective date on signature.

Attached: ATLAS_PO_8372.pdf (PO stub), proforma_schedule.xlsx (requested payment splits).

Can you let me know what approvals are required on your side and whether Redwood can accommodate Net-90 for the first year? If helpful, Ben (CFO) is on copy and can jump in.

Appreciate it,
Emily
Emily Cho
Director, Procurement
Atlas Health

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Emily Cho <emily.cho@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Aug 2026 09:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed invoice schedule for enterprise contract

Hi Emily — thanks for the note and the PO. I’ve looped in Marissa on the commercial side and Marcus on finance to review the ask.

Quick points:
- We can consider a Net-90 or quarterly invoicing for strategic customers, but it needs an exec exception and a documented mitigation (e.g., PO up front, one-time setup fee, or limited credit exposure).
- I’ve attached the proforma you sent to the internal thread and asked for estimated ARR impact and recommended terms.

Marissa / Marcus — can you review Atlas’s stub and propose a clean exception path (pricing adjustment or contractual clause) we should request? Emily, we’ll aim to get an answer by Wednesday.

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
4BB  +1 (415) 555-0138

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Emily Cho <emily.cho@atlashealth.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed invoice schedule for enterprise contract

Thanks for flagging, Evelyn. Reviewed the PO and proforma. A few practical options to present to Atlas:

1) Net-90 for first year only, with a 3% underwriting surcharge (one-time fee rolled into year 1 invoice). Requires exec sign-off.
2) Split into three quarterly invoices (30/30/30 over 90 days) with standard pricing but require PO and signed SOW in advance.
3) Net-60 + 1.5% early-payment discount if they can pay within 60 days (might be attractive to CFO).

From a revenue-recognition and collections perspective Marcus, do we have a preference? If Atlas is strategic and likely to expand, I’d prefer option 1 or 2 to keep the deal moving.

Emily — would Atlas consider the one-time surcharge or the quarterly invoice option if that avoids an exec exception?

Attachments: none (referencing Emily’s uploaded proforma).

Marissa Cole
Director, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Aug 2026 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Exec approval needed: Atlas Health Net-90 request (DW-4027)

Rishi — quick summary: Atlas (prospect converting to customer) has requested Net-90 or quarterly billing for an initial annual committed spend of $420k ARR. They provided PO (attached). Commercial recommends allowance for Net-90 for year 1 with a 3% underwriting surcharge; collections prefers PO up front and quarterly invoices.

Risk note: underwriting exposure ~ $350k outstanding at any given time if fully executed and invoices delayed. Mitigations proposed: PO up front + one-time surcharge or require payment milestones (30/30/30).

Ask: Exec sign-off to approve Net-90 (first-year only) under the conditions below so we can finalize contract and close this quarter.

Proposed approval conditions:
- Net-90 for year 1 only
- PO received and attached to contract as exhibit
- 3% one-time underwriting surcharge on year 1 invoice OR quarterly invoice schedule (customer preference to decide)
- Finance to own collections plan and credit hold if missed payment

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Head of Revenue Ops | Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Aug 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Exec approval needed: Atlas Health Net-90 request (DW-4027)

Thanks for the context — I approve the Net-90 exception for Atlas Health under the following firm conditions:

1) Exception is one-year term only (auto-reverts to standard Net-30 at renewal unless re-approved).
2) PO must be attached to the contract and verified by Finance before first invoice is issued.
3) Apply the 3% underwriting surcharge to the first-year invoice (clearly disclosed on the invoice).
4) Add a clause that allows Redwood to suspend service / pause deployment if payment is more than 15 days overdue beyond Net-90.

Once Marcus confirms the surcharge is applied in the SOW and Finance has validated the PO, Evelyn you have the green light to finalize paperwork and send for signature.

Rishi Malhotra
VP, Commercial Operations | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
